newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kremlin stalls on giving up foreign cars.
newsitem.headline: Kremlin stalls on giving up foreign cars.

text.p: Deputy Premier Boris Nemtsov's dream of forcing Russian officials to dump their foreign cars for local models was dented Monday when Kremlin officials said they had just ordered thousands of new imported sedans.

Nemtsov, whose first act as first deputy prime minister last month was to urge the government to switch to 1970s-style Volgas from his home city of Nizhny Novgorod, insisted Sunday his colleagues were right behind him.
But senior officials said Monday that despite a formal government order inspired by Nemtsov, it would be years before Volgas drove Volvos out of the Kremlin car pool.

A senior official dealing with purchasing for President Boris Yeltsin's administration told Reuters the government had recently signed firm contracts to buy thousands of foreign sedans for Moscow and top regional officials.
Under one contract, Russia would buy about 2,000 Volvo cars from Sweden.
Kommersant Daily newspaper said Saturday the new contracts assumed most of the government's 1,450 cars would be replaced with foreign cars.

Yeltsin favours a blue Mercedes-Benz. Moscow's roads are clogged with government-owned Audis, Saabs, Volvos and Mercedes-Benz cars, jumping traffic jams of coughing Ladas and racing down special lanes once reserved for communist chiefs in frumpy Soviet ZiLs and Volgas.
